messages:
jess: Okay team confession time: I introduced a YAML bug by pasting from a Google Doc that silently converted two spaces into a tab. Spent 45 minutes blaming the runtime. :grimacing:
sam: Been there. The worst part is how innocent the file looks until the linter screams. Tabs are the stealth ninjas of syntax. :ninja:
deploy-bot: deploy #qa-2026-03 triggered rollback: lint error -> yaml: line 8: found tab character that violates indentation
noor: We should add a cheeky PR check that comments: "This tab is on thin ice. Consider converting to spaces."
rahul: Alternative: adopt "tab-first" YAML and watch the world burn. Kidding. Kind of. :fire:
jess: Also this is my reminder to everyone: editorconfig + pre-commit hooks = second brain. Never trust human fingers at 2am.
sam: Proposal: new team ritual — every time CI reports a YAML tab, the reporter gets to request a terrible pun. I'll start: Why did the YAML file go to therapy? Because it had too many unresolved tabs. :crystal_ball:
noor: lol. Also, can we ban emoji in semver tags? I once saw `v2.1.0+party_parrot` and the deploy chart exploded.
rahul: Emoji semver is a power move. Metadata section is just begging for chaos. Imagine `v1.0.0+🚀.coffee`. The migration script would cry.
deploy-bot: Note: tag name `v1.0.0+party_parrot` is allowed by our repo rules but not recommended. Please reference https://example.internal/devops/semver-guidelines
jess: For immediate relief I'm adding a rule to the linter to fail on literal tabs and another rule to warn on emoji in tags. We'll add stickers later.
sam: Sticker idea: "I survived YAML and all I got was this tab-free tee"
noor: I vote for a small trophy for the person who submits the most innocent-looking syntax bug. 
rahul: Winner gets eternal bragging rights and one coffee.
jess: Closing this mini-thread: thanks deploy-bot for the rollback, pre-commit for existing, and everyone for the puns. Moral: trust the linter, not your clipboard. :v:
